summary: Independent verification of Release 6.0.2 Business Partners PR #15 fixes on real PostgreSQL and SQLite. All Codex-review findings appear resolved: (a) farm-scoped read authorization + capabilities + supplier-profile + contacts endpoints — GET works for farm-scoped users in same org, mutations still 403, cross-tenant still 404; (b) audit event completeness — business_partner.create + N contact.create + optional qualification.update with old_/new_ transitions + changed_fields all asserted; (c) supplier profile PATCH before/after audit records; same-state upsert emits no event; (d) ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 validator rejects USA / 1A / X / !! / ZZ / QQ / XX / ZY / lowercase and normalises 'in'->'IN'; nested primary_address country_code also ISO-checked; (e) PATCH null clearing persists NULL for email/phone/job_title/notes; required fields (name/contact_role/is_primary) still 422 on null; (f) IntegrityError → 409 concurrency: dup (org_id, code) race → sorted([201, 409]); capability race → all in {201,409}, never 500 — validated on PostgreSQL; (g) frontend stale-response guard: 2 new tests + 11 baseline pass; (h) tests/test_business_partners.py contains zero '/app/' hardcoded paths — CI portable. Suite counts: SQLite 100 passed + 2 skipped (postgres-only); PostgreSQL 102 passed / 0 skipped (concurrency tests execute). Full API suite on PostgreSQL (excluding BP): 337 passed / 32 skipped (pre-existing sprint4 e2e / sprint5.4.10 DB-layer skips, unrelated). Frontend vitest for business-partners.test.tsx: 13/13 passed.
critical_code_review_comments: Stale-response guard implementation uses a mount ref + generation ref + capturedId comparison (mountedRef/genRef in page.tsx and edit/page.tsx) rather than a literal AbortController as described in the review request. Behaviour is equivalent (stale responses are dropped) and the two vitest tests pass, but the review prose says 'AbortController' — if strict fidelity to the review wording matters, main agent may want to either (a) rename the abstraction or (b) update the review doc to describe the actual guard. Not a bug.

The two @_postgres_only concurrency tests use asyncio.gather on the same in-process AsyncClient session; they exercise the IntegrityError→409 translator but do NOT truly stress advisory-lock ordering under real network parallelism. This is acceptable for a unit-level guarantee that IntegrityError never becomes a 500, but does not fully substitute for a k6/hey style load probe. Documented, not a blocker.

test_concurrent_duplicate_capability_returns_409 accepts both (201, 409) OR (201, 201) — see comment on lines 2173-2175. This is intentional because the pre-check may see both as absent OR one may already commit before the second's flush. Acceptable, but note the assertion is weaker than the code path deserves; a stricter variant that forces the race with a barrier would be nice-to-have.

success_rate.backend: 100% (102/102 BP on PostgreSQL, 100+2-skip on SQLite, 337/337 non-BP full suite on PostgreSQL)
